     9	/// A byte-granular buffer holding data while it is copied.
    10	module idma_dataflow_element #(
    11	    /// The depth of the buffer
    12	    parameter int unsigned BufferDepth = 32'd3,
    13	    /// The width of the buffer in bytes
    14	    parameter int unsigned StrbWidth = 32'd1,
    15	    /// Print the info of the FIFO configuration
    16	    parameter bit PrintFifoInfo = 1'b0,
    17	    /// The strobe type
    18	    parameter type strb_t = logic,
    19	    /// The byte type
    20	    parameter type byte_t = logic [7:0]
    21	)(
    22	    input  logic clk_i,
    23	    input  logic rst_ni,
    24	
    25	    input  byte_t [StrbWidth-1:0] data_i,
    26	    input  strb_t valid_i,
    27	    output strb_t ready_o,
    28	
    29	    output byte_t [StrbWidth-1:0] data_o,
    30	    output strb_t valid_o,
    31	    input  strb_t ready_i
    32	);
    33	
    34	    // buffer is implemented as an array of FIFOs
    35	    for (genvar i = 0; i < StrbWidth; i++) begin : gen_fifo_buffer
    36	        cc_passthrough_stream_fifo #(
    37	            .data_t       ( byte_t        ),
    38	            .Depth        ( BufferDepth   ),
    39	            .PrintInfo    ( PrintFifoInfo )
    40	        ) i_passthrough_stream_fifo (
    41	            .clk_i,
    42	            .rst_ni,
    43	            .clr_i        ( 1'b0        ),
    44	            .flush_i      ( 1'b0        ),
    45	            .data_i       ( data_i  [i] ),
    46	            .valid_i      ( valid_i [i] ),
    47	            .ready_out    ( ready_o [i] ),
    48	            .data_o       ( data_o  [i] ),
    49	            .valid_o      ( valid_o [i] ),
    50	            .ready_i      ( ready_i [i] )
    51	        );
    52	    end : gen_fifo_buffer
    53	
    54	endmodule

    13	module cc_stream_fifo #(
    14	    /// FIFO is in fall-through mode
    15	    parameter bit          FallThrough = 1'b0,
    16	    /// Default data width if the fifo is of type logic
    17	    parameter int unsigned DataWidth   = 32,
    18	    /// Depth can be arbitrary from 0 to 2**32
    19	    parameter int unsigned Depth       = 8,
    20	    parameter type         data_t      = logic [DataWidth-1:0],
    21	    // DO NOT OVERWRITE THIS PARAMETER
    22	    localparam int unsigned UsageWidth = cc_pkg::cnt_width(Depth)
    23	) (
    24	    input  logic                  clk_i,   // Clock
    25	    input  logic                  rst_ni,  // Asynchronous reset active low
    26	    input  logic                  clr_i,   // Synchronous clear active high; clears internal
    27	                                           // pointers *and* memories.
    28	    input  logic                  flush_i, // Flush the queue; compared to clr_i this only clears
    29	                                           // internal pointers. Sufficient for most functional
    30	                                           // purposes.
    31	    output logic [UsageWidth-1:0] usage_o, // Fill pointer
    32	    // input interface
    33	    input  data_t                 data_i,  // Data to push into the fifo
    34	    input  logic                  valid_i, // Input data valid
    35	    output logic                  ready_o, // Fifo is not full
    36	    // output interface
    37	    output data_t                 data_o,  // Output data
    38	    output logic                  valid_o, // Fifo is not empty
    39	    input  logic                  ready_i  // Pop head from fifo
    40	);
    41	
    42	    logic push, pop;
    43	    logic empty, full;
    44	
    45	    assign push    = valid_i & ~full;
    46	    assign pop     = ready_i & ~empty;
    47	    assign ready_o = ~full;
    48	    assign valid_o = ~empty;
    49	
    50	    cc_fifo #(
    51	        .FallThrough(FallThrough),
    52	        .DataWidth  (DataWidth),
    53	        .Depth      (Depth),
    54	        .data_t     (DataWidth)
    55	    ) fifo_i (
    56	        .clk_i,
    57	        .rst_ni,
    58	        .clr_i,
    59	        .flush_i,
    60	        .full_o (full),
    61	        .empty_o(empty),
    62	        .usage_o,
    63	        .data_i,
    64	        .push_i (push),
    65	        .data_o,
    66	        .pop_i  (pop)
    67	    );
    68	
    69	endmodule

    11	
    12	/// Stream FIFO that does not cut the timing path. When full; pushing data is allowed if in
    13	/// the same cycle data is popped. Creates longer timing paths but can use buffer space more
    14	/// efficiently.
    15	module cc_passthrough_stream_fifo #(
    16	    /// Depth can be arbitrary from 2 to 2**32
    17	    parameter int unsigned Depth       = 32'd8,
    18	    /// Print information when the simulation launches
    19	    parameter bit          PrintInfo   = 1'b0,
    20	    /// If the FIFO is full, allow reading and writing in the same cycle
    21	    parameter bit          SameCycleRW = 1'b1,
    22	    /// Type of the FIFO
    23	    parameter type         data_t      = logic
    24	) (
    25	    /// Clock
    26	    input  logic                 clk_i,
    27	    /// Asynchronous reset active low
    28	    input  logic                 rst_ni,
    29	    /// Synchronous clear active high; clears all sequential logic
    30	    input  logic                 clr_i,
    31	    /// Fifo flush. Compared to clr_i, this only clears internal pointers.
    32	    /// Sufficient for most functional purposes.
    33	    input  logic                 flush_i,
    34	    /// data to push into the FIFO
    35	    input  data_t                data_i,
    36	    /// input data valid
    37	    input  logic                 valid_i,
    38	    /// FIFO is not full
    39	    output logic                 ready_o,
    40	    /// output data
    41	    output data_t                data_o,
    42	    /// FIFO is not empty
    43	    output logic                 valid_o,
    44	    /// pop head from FIFO
    45	    input  logic                 ready_i
    46	);
    47	    /// Bit Width of the read and write pointers
    48	    /// One additional bit to detect overflows
    49	    localparam int unsigned PointerWidth = $clog2(Depth) + 1;
    50	
    51	    // Read and write pointers
    52	    logic [PointerWidth-1:0]  read_ptr_d,  read_ptr_q;
    53	    logic [PointerWidth-1:0] write_ptr_d, write_ptr_q;
    54	
    55	    // Data
    56	    data_t [Depth-1:0] data_d, data_q;
    57	
    58	    // Enable storage
    59	    logic load_data;
    60	
    61	    assign data_o = data_q[read_ptr_q[PointerWidth-2:0]];
    62	
    63	    // Logic
    64	    always_comb begin
    65	        // Default
    66	        load_data   = 1'b0;
    67	        read_ptr_d  = read_ptr_q;
    68	        write_ptr_d = write_ptr_q;
    69	        data_d      = data_q;
    70	
    71	        if (flush_i) begin // Flush
    72	            read_ptr_d  = '0;
    73	            write_ptr_d = '0;
    74	            valid_o     = 1'b0;
    75	            ready_o     = 1'b0;
    76	        end else begin
    77	            // Read
    78	            valid_o = read_ptr_q[PointerWidth-1] == write_ptr_q[PointerWidth-1]
    79	                ? read_ptr_q[PointerWidth-2:0] != write_ptr_q[PointerWidth-2:0] : 1'b1;
    80	            if (ready_i && valid_o) begin
    81	                if (read_ptr_q[PointerWidth-2:0] == (Depth-1)) begin
    82	                    // On overflow reset pointer to zero and flip imaginary bit
    83	                    read_ptr_d[PointerWidth-2:0] = '0;
    84	                    read_ptr_d[PointerWidth-1]   = !read_ptr_q[PointerWidth-1];
    85	                end else begin
    86	                    // Increment counter
    87	                    read_ptr_d = read_ptr_q + 'd1;
    88	                end
    89	            end
    90	
    91	            // Write -> Also able to write if we read in the same cycle
    92	            ready_o     = (read_ptr_q[PointerWidth-1] == write_ptr_q[PointerWidth-1]
    93	                ? 1'b1 : write_ptr_q[PointerWidth-2:0] != read_ptr_q[PointerWidth-2:0])
    94	                || (SameCycleRW && ready_i && valid_o);
    95	
    96	            if (valid_i && ready_o) begin
    97	                load_data = 1'b1;
    98	                data_d[write_ptr_q[PointerWidth-2:0]] = data_i;
    99	
   100	                if (write_ptr_q[PointerWidth-2:0] == (Depth-1)) begin
   101	                    // On overflow reset pointer to zero and flip imaginary bit
   102	                    write_ptr_d[PointerWidth-2:0] = '0;
   103	                    write_ptr_d[PointerWidth-1]   = !write_ptr_q[PointerWidth-1];
   104	                end else begin
   105	                    // Increment pointer
   106	                    write_ptr_d = write_ptr_q + 'd1;
   107	                end
   108	            end
   109	        end
   110	    end
   111	
   112	    // Flip Flops
   113	    `FFARNC( read_ptr_q,  read_ptr_d, clr_i, '0, clk_i, rst_ni)
   114	    `FFARNC(write_ptr_q, write_ptr_d, clr_i, '0, clk_i, rst_ni)
   115	
   116	    `FFLARNC(data_q, data_d, load_data, clr_i, '0, clk_i, rst_ni)
   117	
   118	endmodule

    16	module cc_fifo #(
    17	    parameter bit          FallThrough = 1'b0, // fifo is in fall-through mode
    18	    parameter int unsigned DataWidth   = 32,   // default data width if the fifo is of type logic
    19	    parameter int unsigned Depth       = 8,    // depth can be arbitrary from 0 to 2**32
    20	    parameter type         data_t      = logic [DataWidth-1:0],
    21	    // DO NOT OVERWRITE THIS PARAMETER
    22	    localparam int unsigned UsageWidth = cc_pkg::cnt_width(Depth)
    23	)(
    24	    input  logic  clk_i,   // Clock
    25	    input  logic  rst_ni,  // Asynchronous reset active low
    26	    input  logic  clr_i,   // Synchronous clear active high; clears internal pointers *and*
    27	                           // memories.
    28	    input  logic  flush_i, // Flush the queue; compared to clr_i this only clears internal pointers.
    29	                           // Sufficient for most functional purposes.
    30	    // Status flags
    31	    output logic  full_o,  // Queue is full
    32	    output logic  empty_o, // Queue is empty
    33	    output logic  [UsageWidth-1:0] usage_o,  // Fill pointer
    34	    // As long as the queue is not full we can push new data
    35	    input  data_t data_i,  // Data to push into the queue
    36	    input  logic  push_i,  // Data is valid and can be pushed to the queue
    37	    // As long as the queue is not empty we can pop new elements
    38	    output data_t data_o,  // Output data
    39	    input  logic  pop_i    // Pop head from queue
    40	);
    41	    // local parameter
    42	    // FIFO depth - handle the case of pass-through, synthesizer will do constant propagation
    43	    localparam int unsigned FifoDepth = (Depth > 0) ? Depth : 1;
    44	    localparam int unsigned PtrWidth = cc_pkg::idx_width(Depth);
    45	    // clock gating control
    46	    logic gate_clock;
    47	    // pointer to the read and write section of the queue
    48	    logic [PtrWidth-1:0] read_pointer_n, read_pointer_q, write_pointer_n, write_pointer_q;
    49	    // keep a counter to keep track of the current queue status
    50	    // this integer will be truncated by the synthesis tool
    51	    logic [UsageWidth-1:0] status_cnt_n, status_cnt_q;
    52	    // actual memory
    53	    data_t [FifoDepth - 1:0] mem_n, mem_q;
    54	
    55	    assign usage_o = status_cnt_q;
    56	
    57	    if (Depth == 0) begin : gen_pass_through
    58	        assign empty_o     = ~push_i;
    59	        assign full_o      = ~pop_i;
    60	    end else begin : gen_fifo
    61	        assign full_o       = (status_cnt_q == FifoDepth[UsageWidth-1:0]);
    62	        assign empty_o      = (status_cnt_q == 0) & ~(FallThrough & push_i);
    63	    end
    64	    // status flags
    65	
    66	    // read and write queue logic
    67	    always_comb begin : read_write_comb
    68	        // default assignment
    69	        read_pointer_n  = read_pointer_q;
    70	        write_pointer_n = write_pointer_q;
    71	        status_cnt_n    = status_cnt_q;
    72	        data_o          = (Depth == 0) ? data_i : mem_q[read_pointer_q];
    73	        mem_n           = mem_q;
    74	        gate_clock      = 1'b1;
    75	
    76	        // push a new element to the queue
    77	        if (push_i && ~full_o) begin
    78	            // push the data onto the queue
    79	            mem_n[write_pointer_q] = data_i;
    80	            // un-gate the clock, we want to write something
    81	            gate_clock = 1'b0;
    82	            // increment the write counter
    83	            // this is dead code when Depth is a power of two
    84	            if (write_pointer_q == FifoDepth[PtrWidth-1:0] - 1)
    85	                write_pointer_n = '0;
    86	            else
    87	                write_pointer_n = write_pointer_q + 1;
    88	            // increment the overall counter
    89	            status_cnt_n    = status_cnt_q + 1;
    90	        end
    91	
    92	        if (pop_i && ~empty_o) begin
    93	            // read from the queue is a default assignment
    94	            // but increment the read pointer...
    95	            // this is dead code when Depth is a power of two
    96	            if (read_pointer_n == FifoDepth[PtrWidth-1:0] - 1)
    97	                read_pointer_n = '0;
    98	            else
    99	                read_pointer_n = read_pointer_q + 1;
   100	            // ... and decrement the overall count
   101	            status_cnt_n   = status_cnt_q - 1;
   102	        end
   103	
   104	        // keep the count pointer stable if we push and pop at the same time
   105	        if (push_i && pop_i &&  ~full_o && ~empty_o)
   106	            status_cnt_n   = status_cnt_q;
   107	
   108	        // FIFO is in pass through mode -> do not change the pointers
   109	        if (FallThrough && (status_cnt_q == 0) && push_i) begin
   110	            data_o = data_i;
   111	            if (pop_i) begin
   112	                status_cnt_n = status_cnt_q;
   113	                read_pointer_n = read_pointer_q;
   114	                write_pointer_n = write_pointer_q;
   115	            end
   116	        end
   117	    end
   118	
   119	    // sequential process
   120	    logic clr_or_flush;
   121	    assign clr_or_flush = clr_i || flush_i;
   122	    `FFARNC(read_pointer_q, read_pointer_n, clr_or_flush, '0, clk_i, rst_ni)
   123	    `FFARNC(write_pointer_q, write_pointer_n, clr_or_flush, '0, clk_i, rst_ni)
   124	    `FFARNC(status_cnt_q, status_cnt_n, clr_or_flush, '0, clk_i, rst_ni)
   125	
   126	    `FFLARNC(mem_q, mem_n, !gate_clock, clr_or_flush, {FifoDepth{data_t'('0)}}, clk_i, rst_ni)
   127	
   128	`ifndef COMMON_CELLS_ASSERTS_OFF
   129	    `ASSERT_INIT(depth_0, Depth > 0, "Depth must be greater than 0.")
   130	
   131	    `ASSERT(full_write, full_o |-> ~push_i, clk_i, !rst_ni,
   132	            "Trying to push new data although the FIFO is full.")
   133	
   134	    `ASSERT(empty_read, empty_o |-> ~pop_i, clk_i, !rst_ni,
   135	            "Trying to pop data although the FIFO is empty.")
   136	`endif
   137	
   138	endmodule // cc_fifo

    15	  /// Ceiled Division of Two Natural Numbers
    16	  ///
    17	  /// Returns the quotient of two natural numbers, rounded towards plus infinity.
    18	  function automatic longint unsigned ceil_div (
    19	    input longint unsigned dividend,
    20	    input longint unsigned divisor
    21	  );
    22	    automatic longint unsigned quotient = 0;
    23	
    24	    `ifndef SYNTHESIS
    25	    `ifndef COMMON_CELLS_ASSERTS_OFF
    26	    if (divisor == 0) begin
    27	      $fatal(1, "Division by zero!");
    28	    end
    29	    `endif
    30	    `endif
    31	
    32	    quotient = dividend / divisor;
    33	    if ((dividend % divisor) != 0) begin
    34	      quotient++;
    35	    end
    36	
    37	    return quotient;
    38	  endfunction

    40	  /// Index width required to be able to represent up to `num_idx` indices as a binary
    41	  /// encoded signal.
    42	  /// Ensures that the minimum width if an index signal is `1`, regardless of parametrization.
    43	  function automatic int unsigned idx_width (input int unsigned num_idx);
    44	    if (num_idx > 32'd1) begin
    45	      return unsigned'($clog2(num_idx));
    46	    end else begin
    47	      return 32'd1;
    48	    end
    49	  endfunction

    51	  /// Count width required to represent all count values from `0` to `max_cnt`, inclusive.
    52	  function automatic int unsigned cnt_width (input int unsigned max_cnt);
    53	    return idx_width(max_cnt + 1);
    54	  endfunction

    56	  /// Checks if a value is a power of 2 (and is not 0)
    57	  /// Returns 1 if the input value is a power of 2, else 0
    58	  function automatic bit is_power_of_2 (input int unsigned value);
    59	    automatic int unsigned value_without_lowest_set_bit;
    60	
    61	    if (value == 32'd0) begin
    62	      return 1'b0;
    63	    end
    64	
    65	    value_without_lowest_set_bit = value & (value - 32'd1);
    66	    return (value_without_lowest_set_bit == 32'd0);
    67	  endfunction

    71	    if (width != 32'd0) begin

    73	    end else begin

   114	  // Calculate required ECC parity width:
   115	  function automatic int unsigned ecc_get_parity_width (input int unsigned data_width);
   116	    // data_width + cw_width + 1 <= 2**cw_width
   117	    int unsigned cw_width = 2;
   118	    while (unsigned'(2**cw_width) < cw_width + data_width + 1) cw_width++;

    41	// Flip-Flop with asynchronous active-low reset
    42	// __q: Q output of FF
    43	// __d: D input of FF
    44	// __reset_value: value assigned upon reset
    45	// (__clk: clock input)
    46	// (__arst_n: asynchronous reset, active-low)
    47	`define FF(__q, __d, __reset_value, __clk = `REG_DFLT_CLK, __arst_n = `REG_DFLT_RST_N) \
    48	  always_ff @(posedge (__clk) or negedge (__arst_n)) begin                             \
    49	    if (!__arst_n) begin                                                               \
    50	      __q <= (__reset_value);                                                          \
    51	    end else begin                                                                     \
    52	      __q <= (__d);                                                                    \
    53	    end                                                                                \
    54	  end

    59	// __reset_value: value assigned upon reset

    63	  always_ff @(posedge (__clk) or posedge (__arst)) begin                             \
    64	    if (__arst) begin                                                                \
    65	      __q <= (__reset_value);                                                        \
    66	    end else begin                                                                   \
    67	      __q <= (__d);                                                                  \

item.text: The configured source set exposes three local compile-time faults before full elaboration: the packet FIFO passes a value where `cc_fifo.data_t` requires a type, and the generated lane FIFO uses a nonexistent `ready_out` port (leaving its actual `ready_o` unconnected). I’m now separating those definite integration defects from the FIFO storage behavior and the intentionally unavailable monitor.

Not ready for integration sign-off. The intended lane/beat types and requested depths are configured correctly, but two local SystemVerilog/interface errors and one packet-FIFO flush behavior violate the requirements.

Local-source findings:

- `lane_t` is a packed 13-bit struct (8-bit payload, 4-bit tag, poison), and `beat_t` is a packed 39-bit three-lane type at [integration.sv:2](/private/tmp/slang-compare-open/runs/idma_review/mcp+skill/rep_1/workspace/integration.sv:2). Slang resolved the top `data_i`/`data_o` as 39-bit with no unpacked dimensions.

- The intended capacity/type chain is correct at the outer instances: `compare_idma_state.i_dataflow` has `BufferDepth=5`, `StrbWidth=3`, and `byte_t=lane_t` at [integration.sv:31](/private/tmp/slang-compare-open/runs/idma_review/mcp+skill/rep_1/workspace/integration.sv:31). All three generated lane FIFOs resolve to depth 5 and lane type. `compare_idma_state.i_packet_fifo` resolves to `Depth=5`, `FallThrough=1'b1`, and `data_t=beat_t` at [integration.sv:39](/private/tmp/slang-compare-open/runs/idma_review/mcp+skill/rep_1/workspace/integration.sv:39). Thus the requested fall-through setting is preserved in the parameter chain.

- The lane valid/ready path is currently invalid. `idma_dataflow_element` connects `.ready_out(...)` at [idma_dataflow_element.sv:47](/private/tmp/slang-compare-open/runs/idma_review/mcp+skill/rep_1/workspace/rtl/src/backend/idma_dataflow_element.sv:47), but `cc_passthrough_stream_fifo` declares its output as `ready_o` at [cc_passthrough_stream_fifo.sv:39](/private/tmp/slang-compare-open/runs/idma_review/mcp+skill/rep_1/workspace/rtl/.bender/git/checkouts/common_cells-b5ef1d9e9e7e3ce8/src/cc_passthrough_stream_fifo.sv:39). Slang reports `PortDoesNotExist` and confirms all three generated FIFO `ready_o` ports are unconnected. Consequently, the top-level `ready_o = &lane_ready` at [integration.sv:29](/private/tmp/slang-compare-open/runs/idma_review/mcp+skill/rep_1/workspace/integration.sv:29) cannot provide a valid handshake. Change that association to `.ready_o(ready_o[i])`.

- The packet FIFO is not legal SystemVerilog as written. `cc_stream_fifo` passes `DataWidth`—an integer—to `cc_fifo`’s type parameter at [cc_stream_fifo.sv:54](/private/tmp/slang-compare-open/runs/idma_review/mcp+skill/rep_1/workspace/rtl/.bender/git/checkouts/common_cells-b5ef1d9e9e7e3ce8/src/cc_stream_fifo.sv:54). Slang reports `NotAType`, and the inner packet FIFO’s `data_t` resolves as an error. Change this to `.data_t(data_t)`. That preserves the structured `beat_t`; substituting a raw 39-bit vector would not meet the type-preservation requirement.

- Clear and flush are correctly bound from the top at [integration.sv:42](/private/tmp/slang-compare-open/runs/idma_review/mcp+skill/rep_1/workspace/integration.sv:42). In `cc_fifo`, `clr_or_flush = clr_i || flush_i` resets the read pointer, write pointer, and occupancy at [cc_fifo.sv:120](/private/tmp/slang-compare-open/runs/idma_review/mcp+skill/rep_1/workspace/rtl/.bender/git/checkouts/common_cells-b5ef1d9e9e7e3ce8/src/cc_fifo.sv:120)-[cc_fifo.sv:124](/private/tmp/slang-compare-open/runs/idma_review/mcp+skill/rep_1/workspace/rtl/.bender/git/checkouts/common_cells-b5ef1d9e9e7e3ce8/src/cc_fifo.sv:124), as required. However, that same signal clears `mem_q` at [cc_fifo.sv:126](/private/tmp/slang-compare-open/runs/idma_review/mcp+skill/rep_1/workspace/rtl/.bender/git/checkouts/common_cells-b5ef1d9e9e7e3ce8/src/cc_fifo.sv:126). The register macro gives clear priority over a write, so a flush zeroes payload storage and prevents an otherwise enabled write. This fails the flush requirement.

  Minimal correction: retain `clr_or_flush` for pointers and occupancy, but pass only `clr_i` as the memory-clear input in the `FFLARNC(mem_q, ...)` invocation. Then clear still wipes payload, flush only empties the queue state, ordinary writes can update storage during flush, and low `rst_ni` still resets storage.

External boundary:

`config.json` explicitly marks `idma_boundary_monitor` unavailable, and Slang reports it unknown at [integration.sv:46](/private/tmp/slang-compare-open/runs/idma_review/mcp+skill/rep_1/workspace/integration.sv:46). Its implementation and monitor-specific checks cannot be assessed here; no replacement should be invented. The two local compile errors are independent of that expected missing component.

No files were modified.
